messages:
Sam W: Heads up — CI job linux-x86_64/runtime-tests is red on an intermittent unit: serve_retry_test. Fails ~1/20 runs, looks timing-related. Logs attached below.

Dev CI Bot: CI job #5123 failed on linux-x86_64 (tests/runtime). Rerun/hint: use --test_output=errors to see failure.

Alex K: Hmm, could be mock clock vs real timer jitter. Any stacktrace or failing assertion?

Maya P: Can you paste the minimal failing log + the test name exact args?

Sam W: Sure — here's the top of the failure (trimmed):
```
thread 'serve_retry_test' panicked at 'expected no retry after success', runtime/src/serve/retry.rs:142:21
...
assertion failed: elapsed < Duration::from_millis(100)
actual elapsed: 143ms
```
Test is flaky when run under CI container with concurrent jobs.

Thomas L: Repro steps to try locally: `bazel test //runtime:serve_tests --test_output=errors --test_arg=--nocapture` and run with single thread `RAYON_NUM_THREADS=1` to rule out scheduling noise.

Sam W: Kicked off a rerun first: `ci rerun 5123`.

Dev CI Bot: Rerun #5123.1 finished — still failing. Same assertion.

Maya P: If rerun still red, let's bisect on recent change that touched retry/timer. Any suspect commits?

Alex K: Two recent commits touched timer resolution and prefetch paths: 9f3c2 (kv-prefetch) and a71b9 (retry backoff). My money is on backoff scheduling change.

Thomas L: Another quick check: try pinning test seed/shuffle so we can reproduce deterministically. For the Rust tests add env `RUST_TEST_THREADS=1` and run with `--test-threads=1` and `--nocapture`. Also try `RUST_BACKTRACE=1`.

Sam W: Running local loop now: `for i in {1..200}; do cargo test serve_retry_test -- --test-threads=1 --nocapture || break; done`. Hit fail on run 37 locally. Uploading the failing run log to the thread.

Maya P: Nice repro. Can you capture the timing around the retry window? Maybe add a temporary debug log in test to print start/stop timestamps.

Sam W: Added debug prints and pushed a branch `sam/debug-retry-timing` with the extra logs + a flaky guard. Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2894

Thomas L: If you can reproduce reliably, try running under `perf` or `strace` to see if we get any syscall delays. But first try increasing the allowed tolerance to confirm it's a timing flake not logic bug.

Alex K: We should avoid widening timeouts permanently. If tolerance increase makes it stable, then we know it's scheduling jitter and need a robust mock clock or deterministic timers for the test.

eng-runtime-oncall: I'll spin up a CI debug job pinned to a single vCPU and no other noisy containers to see if it still flakes. Tagging infra to allow debug job.

Sam W: Thanks — will re-run against debug job when it's ready. :thumbsup:

Dev CI Bot: Debug job request #dbg-78 created. You'll get logs at: https://ci.internal/redwood/jobs/dbg-78

Sam W: Ran against dbg-78 — test passed 50/50 locally but passed in debug job once. Uploading debug job logs.

Maya P: Mixed results — suggests race with other tests or CPU contention in standard CI workers. Can we isolate the test to run in its own sandbox job?

Thomas L: Suggestion: add `#[serial]` or run test in exclusive mode in CI pipeline while we root cause. Then open a follow-up to replace real timers with a fake clock for the retry path.

Sam W: Will open an exclusive CI job for this test and add a temporary `#[ignore]` + an issue tracking the proper fix if it repros more.

Alex K: Thanks. If you get a deterministic repro, ping me and I'll run a bisection on the two suspect commits.

Sam W: Will do. Current plan: (1) exclusive CI job, (2) temp debug logs + repro attempts, (3) bisect commits if repro deterministic, (4) either mock clock or fix scheduling in retry code.

Maya P: Sounds good. Keep thread updated and assign the PR when you have a reproducer.

Sam W: Update: created issue #3982 and a short-lived flaky marker on CI to stop noisy alerts. Dropping the exclusive job in 48h if green.

eng-runtime-oncall: Noted. If it spikes again I'll promote to a hotfix.

Sam W: thanks everyone.
